perf.summary: Convert recursive Query into an iterative loop to eliminate per-level call overhead on the hottest path
perf.currentCost: Query is O(log n) recursion, invoked once per Find iteration and Find runs in a loop (multiple Query calls per Union). Each segment-tree level costs a full method call: argument marshaling of 8 parameters (root,l,r,idx,parent,lc,rc,size + out s), return-address push, stack frame setup. The out parameter 's' forces a store through a pointer at the leaf. The dependency chain is call -> load lc/rc[root] -> compare -> recurse.
perf.proposedChange: Rewrite as: int node=root; while(l!=r){ int mid=(l+r)>>1; if(idx<=mid){ node=lc[node]; r=mid; } else { node=rc[node]; l=mid+1; } } s=size[node]; return parent[node]; Keep the public signature identical so callers are unchanged.
perf.rationale: Tail-style descent has no need for a stack; the loop turns N recursive frames into N cheap iterations with one branch and one pointer load each, shrinking the dependency chain and removing call/return overhead. Burst/JIT may already tail-call-optimize this, but an explicit loop guarantees it and avoids the out-pointer store happening once per leaf only.
perf.risk: None — observable behavior is identical for all valid idx in [l,r]. The leaf assignment to s happens exactly once (at the leaf) as before. No signed/overflow change: (l+r)>>1 semantics unchanged.

perf.summary: Inline the segment-tree descent into Find to fuse the Find loop with Query traversal
perf.currentCost: Find calls Query (a full O(log n) traversal) on every loop iteration just to read parent[x] and size[x] for the current x. Each iteration re-enters the tree at root and walks down again. The out-int s is written every iteration but only the final value is used by the caller (sa/sb in Union). So intermediate s stores are wasted work, and every iteration pays full call overhead plus an out-pointer store.
perf.proposedChange: Inline an iterative descent inside Find's while(true): walk node from root using idx=x to the leaf, set p=parent[leaf]; only write s=size[leaf] when p==x (the terminal iteration), then return. This fuses the two loops, drops the Query call entirely, and removes the per-iteration s store for non-terminal steps.
perf.rationale: Eliminates one function call per Find iteration and avoids repeatedly storing through the out pointer 's' for intermediate (discarded) values — only the final size matters to callers. Fewer instructions per iteration and a shorter dependency chain; better Burst codegen since there is no out-parameter aliasing to reason about each step.
perf.risk: Must preserve that s reflects size of the final representative x (the node where parent==x). Guard: only assign s on the returning iteration. Behavior identical to current code, which returns size of the last queried node (the representative). No edge-case change for self-roots (first query returns p==x with its own size).

perf.summary: Mark hot leaf descent helpers with [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]
perf.currentCost: Query, Swap, and (if kept) the descent helpers are separate methods. Query is called from Find in a tight loop; Swap is called twice in Union. Without an inlining hint the JIT/Burst may keep them as out-of-line calls, adding call/return overhead on the hot Find path.
perf.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to Query (once iterative) and to Swap. The using for System.Runtime.CompilerServices is already present.
perf.rationale: AggressiveInlining on small leaf methods lets Burst fold them into callers, removing call overhead and enabling cross-method register allocation and constant propagation of l/r/mid. Swap is two-temp trivial and benefits from inlining into Union.
perf.risk: None functionally. Inlining a recursive Query has no effect (recursion isn't inlined), so this hint only pays off if Query is first made iterative (see other opportunity).

perf.summary: Branchless size-ordered swap to avoid a mispredictable branch before Update
perf.currentCost: if (sa < sb) { Swap(ref ra,ref rb); Swap(ref sa,ref sb); } is a data-dependent branch on union sizes, which is essentially random in DSU workloads and thus frequently mispredicted (~15-20 cycle penalty per misprediction).
perf.proposedChange: Replace with branchless conditional select: int lt=-(sa<sb?1:0) is still a branch in C#; instead compute mask via comparison and arithmetic select, or simply ensure (ra,sa) is the larger root using max/min-style select: e.g. int swap=(sa<sb)?1:0; then use it without a control-flow branch is hard in C#. Lower-risk: keep the branch but note it is cold relative to Find/Update cost (each Update is O(log n)).
perf.rationale: Removing an unpredictable branch saves misprediction penalties; however the surrounding Find+Update work is O(log n) and dominates, so the swap branch is a small fraction of Union cost.
perf.risk: C# lacks a clean branchless 2-tuple swap without cmov-style intrinsics; a naive bit-mask select on ra/rb/sa/sb is correct but verbose. Given Update dominates, this is low-impact — only pursue if profiling later shows Union branch cost. Marked low and optional to avoid cargo-cult.

perf.summary: Build recursion depth and node count are fine; no scratch buffers, but note stack depth is O(n) due to left-recursion pattern
perf.currentCost: Build recurses depth O(log n) for a balanced tree (Build(l,mid) then Build(mid+1,r)), which is acceptable. allocCnt is dereferenced via pointer (*allocCnt) once per node — a load+store through a pointer each call, plus it aliases nothing else so it's cheap. No real RAM waste here.
perf.proposedChange: Optionally pass allocCnt by ref int instead of int* if callers can supply a ref, avoiding pointer-aliasing assumptions and letting Burst keep the counter in a register across the recursion; or hoist *allocCnt into a local counter threaded by return value. Low priority given correctness and existing pointer-based API.
perf.rationale: A ref/register-resident counter avoids repeated memory round-trips through allocCnt, but the recursive structure means the increment must be visible across sibling calls, so it must live in memory or be threaded through return values — the current pointer approach is already the simplest correct form.
perf.risk: Changing allocCnt from int* to ref int alters the public API signature (ergonomics/breaking) and Burst treats both similarly for an escaping address. Net win is marginal; flag only, do not force. No semantic change if done carefully.
